Subject: PoC trial plan: deployment mode discussion (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) - Acme Corp

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have a single source of truth:

Summary of what we heard from Acme:
- Primary objective: validate model performance and cost economics for your customer-facing summarization feature.
- Deployment preferences: leaning toward Redwood Dedicated for predictable throughput, but security/PHI concerns may push you to Private (VPC/on-prem).
- Key stakeholders: Sarah Li (CTO), Mike Torres (Infra lead), Angela Park (Security/compliance).

Proposed PoC/trial plan (high level):
1) Scope: 2 endpoints (summarize, chat-complete) with representative traffic (sanitized sample).
2) Success criteria (mutually agreed):
   - Latency: p95 < 150ms for summarize endpoint under baseline load (10 req/s).
   - Throughput: sustain 10 req/s steady state, 50 req/s burst for 60s.
   - Quality: automated evals on 500 prompt pairs — precision/recall thresholds to be defined with your PM.
   - Cost target: target unit economics < $0.02 per 1k tokens processed (estimate for budgeting).
3) Timeline:
   - Kickoff: week of Dec 13 (we suggested Dec 14 10:00 PT, pending confirmation).
   - Provisioning: Dedicated capacity can be standing up within ~48 hours once capacity is approved; Private/VPC requires network timeline (see below).
   - Trial duration: 3 weeks of controlled traffic + 1 week for wrap-up and reporting.
4) Stakeholder responsibilities:
   - Acme: provide sanitized dataset, test account, network contact for VPC peering (if testing Private), procurement point-of-contact for PO.
   - Redwood: provide Dedicated trial nodes, SRE support for provisioning, evaluation scripts, SOC 2 and security artifacts.

Open items / asks from Acme:
- Confirm preferred deployment mode for the PoC (Dedicated vs Private). If you want us to proceed with Dedicated for speed and then evaluate Private, we can do a two-phase approach.
- Confirm availability for kickoff (we suggested Dec 14 10:00 PT).
- Provide procurement contact and any PO/contract constraints (NDA/SLA).

Attachments: PoC plan draft attached — 20261201-jordan-poc-plan-acme.pdf (contains detailed success criteria and test schedule).
Related links: HubSpot deal: https://redwood.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4567; SOC2 report: https://drive.redwood.com/soc2-report; DocuSign PO template (provisional): https://app.docusign.com/ACME-POC-1234

If this looks right I’ll schedule the kickoff and loop in Marissa to run the technical onboarding.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com

We’d consider a two-phase PoC: Dedicated first for baseline performance, then Private to validate network/residency requirements.
- Cost comparison: please include a 3-week cost estimate for Dedicated vs Private (high-level and callouts for any setup fees).
- Data: we will provide a sanitized sample dataset (non-PII) for the test — estimate delivery by Dec 10.
- Procurement: I’ll introduce our procurement lead (POC: priya.kumar@acmecorp.com) separately. We have standard security addenda and a SOC2 review checklist — can you share the checklist and expected evidence?

Availability: Dec 14 10:00 PT should work for our leads. Please send a calendar invite and agenda (60m).

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Hi all —

Quick technical notes from the solutions side to help planning:

1) Dedicated option (fastest):
   - We can provision a Dedicated pool sized for your trial (recommended starting config: 2x A100-80GB nodes, consistent KV cache across nodes).
   - Typical provisioning time is ~24–48 hours after approval and billing setup.
   - No network changes required on Acme side for Dedicated (traffic runs over TLS to our hosted endpoints).

2) Private / VPC option (security-forward):
   - Private requires VPC peering or PrivateLink and an SRE window to configure routes/ACLs. Expect 1–2 weeks of network coordination if your infra team is ready.
   - On-prem agent available for air-gapped scenarios; that path requires additional lead time and signed support agreement.

3) PoC scope suggestion (practical):
   - Phase 1 (week 1–3): Dedicated trial with production-like traffic (sanitized). Focus on latency, throughput, and quality evals.
   - Phase 2 (optional, week 4–6): If security gating requires it, replicate configuration in Private VPC to validate residency and audit logs.

4) Success criteria (technical hooks):
   - SLOs: p95 latency < 150ms for summarize endpoint on Dedicated.
   - Traces: Redwood will provide per-request tracing + token-level cost reports for the trial.
   - Logging/audit: for Private we can enable extended audit retention and KMS integration.

I’ve attached a simple architecture sketch (poc-aws-arch.png) showing Dedicated vs VPC data flows. I’ll be on the kickoff to run the onboarding and install evaluation harness.

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
